title: corrosion-probes-report-to-the-watch
intention: Every standing WATCHME probe berthed in cairn/machines/corrosion reports to harbor_master's watch verb with {ticket, holds, finding} stated against its own ticket's falsifier, and each spec names that receiver.
why: Every standing probe in cairn/machines/corrosion mails with no verb and nothing uses it (835b5736bf2b D2); a88d6a368cfb built the watch verb that uses a WATCHME finding and 8ecb99998254 built watch_carry. Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a: build the receivers.
traces_to: 835b5736bf2b's falsifier (zero probe-bearing standing specs lack a receiver) and Akien's answer to open-291189a9766a; the 2026-09-30 ruling that a probe's data must have a consumer that USES it; RULE 1 (the build stays inside cairn/machines/corrosion; base's helper through its public interface, harbor_master through its bus verb)
how: Measured 2026-10-03: 2 tickets at a rest carry a watchme probe under cairn/machines/corrosion/probes/ (075cccec5b5d, 50fb8e941f00). Read 2026-10-03: two standing tickets carry a probe under cairn/machines/corrosion/probes, both posting to='harbor_master' with no verb, both fails-shaped: plaster_is_caught_not_argued (075cccec5b5d) is TRUE while no genuine_catch.json marker exists under corrosion's instance — the corrosion sieve has never had a catch dispositioned; the_comparison_is_read (50fb8e941f00) is TRUE once 20+ build_inspector run records exist and no comparison_acted.json marker does. Grep 2026-10-03 of cairn, skills, bin and launchers: nothing outside the probes writes either marker, so when a probe fires its finding is honest and its ticket goes to FIXME — which is where the missing marker writer gets built; that is the receiver USING the data, not the unreceivable case (d48d54dccde6's probe reads input files that are its data, and it can never post anything true). No proof imports either probe. Each PROBE gets verb='watch' and carry=watch_carry(<its id>, _carry, <its predicate>), importing watch_carry from cairn.tools.base.probe (declared public). Each ticket's watchme spec gains receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} through the artifact door. A proof under cairn/machines/corrosion/proofs reads the population from the commons and asserts each probe's verb, to, and live payload invariants.
falsifier: GREEN when every ticket at PROVED or WATCHME whose watchme.probe sits under cairn/machines/corrosion has a probe whose PROBE posts verb 'watch' to 'harbor_master' and whose payload over live data carries ticket == that ticket's id, holds a bool, and a non-empty finding whenever holds is False; and every such spec names receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} with watchme_spec_error naming no receiver fault. RED if any standing corrosion spec lacks the receiver, or if a converted payload's ticket is a path or another id. WRONG INTENT if a corrosion probe's data has a reader other than its own ticket's FIXME that only Akien could name.
watchme: none, because what this child's probes say is read by harbor_master's watch verb (a88d6a368cfb, PROVED), and whether they ever fire is 164da559823d's and acb4ecd84364's watch (CairnCommons/tickets/164da559823d-*.json); a probe on probes reporting would need a receiver of its own.
children: none, because the change is 2 PROBE declarations and their specs, all inside cairn/machines/corrosion.
builder_notes: A Haiku builder would ask: (1) Which probes and how: 075cccec5b5d plaster_is_caught_not_argued (fails=_trigger), 50fb8e941f00 the_comparison_is_read (fails=_trigger). In each file under cairn/machines/corrosion/probes/: append watch_carry to the existing 'from cairn.tools.base.probe import ...' line; use the probe's id constant (named per probe below, added as `_TICKET_ID = "<id>"` after the import block when absent); in PROBE = Probe(...) replace 'carry=_carry,' with 'verb="watch",' and 'carry=watch_carry(<const>, _carry, <pred>),'. Neither probe holds its ticket id in a constant (the slug is only in the docstring), so each gains _TICKET_ID carrying the 12-hex id for watch_carry. Nothing else in a probe changes. (2) watch_carry exists in cairn/tools/base/probe.py (8ecb99998254); do not edit it. (3) Specs: each ticket's watchme spec whose probe starts with cairn/machines/corrosion/probes/ gains receiver {what: 'harbor_master watch verb', in: 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'}, through cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write. (4) Proof: cairn/machines/corrosion/proofs/test_corrosion_probes_report_to_the_watch.py, PROVES {'6c75219037b5': {'all': 'test_corrosion_probes_report_to_the_watch'}}, modeled on cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py. (5) Every proof that imports a converted probe stays green: run them.

decisions.text: D1: the probes — In each of these files under cairn/machines/corrosion/probes/: plaster_is_caught_not_argued.py (075cccec5b5d: constant _TICKET_ID — add it; fails=_trigger), the_comparison_is_read.py (50fb8e941f00: constant _TICKET_ID — add it; fails=_trigger) — append watch_carry to the existing `from cairn.tools.base.probe import ...` line; where the constant is to be added, add `_TICKET_ID = "<its id>"` after the import block; in `PROBE = Probe(...)` replace `carry=_carry,` with `verb="watch",` and `carry=watch_carry(<constant>, _carry, <its predicate>),`. Neither probe holds its ticket id in a constant (the slug is only in the docstring), so each gains _TICKET_ID carrying the 12-hex id for watch_carry. Nothing else changes; watch_carry is not edited.

D3: the proof — Create cairn/machines/corrosion/proofs/test_corrosion_probes_report_to_the_watch.py: a copy of cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/test_inference_probes_report_to_the_watch.py with the docstring naming cairn/machines/corrosion and ticket 6c75219037b5; PROVES = {'6c75219037b5': {'all': 'test_corrosion_probes_report_to_the_watch'}}; BERTH = 'cairn/machines/corrosion/probes/'; _REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4] (the repo root: the directory holding cairn/); teeth renamed test_every_standing_corrosion_probe_posts_watch, test_every_standing_corrosion_spec_names_the_receiver and the composite test_corrosion_probes_report_to_the_watch. Structure, in full: imports importlib, json, subprocess, sys, Path; _REPO_ROOT on sys.path; parse_workflow from cairn.tools.base.transitions; watchme_spec_error from cairn.tools.base.watchme_spec; _main_tree() = Path(git -C _REPO_ROOT rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir).parent falling back to _REPO_ROOT; _tickets() = _main_tree().parent/'CairnCommons'/'tickets'; _standing() = (id, doc, spec) for each ticket at PROVED or WATCHME whose watchme spec's probe starts with BERTH, asserting non-empty; the posts tooth imports each probe module and asserts PROBE.verb == 'watch', PROBE.to == 'harbor_master', payload({}) carries ticket == the id, holds a bool, non-empty finding when holds is False (invariants only); the receiver tooth asserts spec['receiver'] == {'what': 'harbor_master watch verb', 'in': 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'} and watchme_spec_error(doc) names no receiver fault; a __main__ block runs each, prints PASS/FAIL, exits 1 on any failure. No classes.

D4: the specs' receiver — Ticket files are /home/akien/dev/src/CairnCommons/tickets/<id>-<slug>.json (glob '<id>-*.json', exactly one). For each of 075cccec5b5d, 50fb8e941f00: doc = json.loads(Path(p).read_text()); the watchme is a dict or list of dicts; the spec whose 'probe' starts with 'cairn/machines/corrosion/probes/' gets spec['receiver'] = {'what': 'harbor_master watch verb', 'in': 'cairn/devices/cairn/machines/harbor_master'}; then cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(p, json.dumps(doc, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n', verb='cast', why='<id>: the watchme names its receiver, harbor_master\'s watch verb (6c75219037b5)') — write(path, text, *, verb, why), text the WHOLE modified ticket. Run it as a script file (a shell command naming a record path and writing is refused by the artifact gate).

D5: green, seal, commit — Run cairn/machines/corrosion/proofs/test_corrosion_probes_report_to_the_watch.py (exit 0) and the probe-importing proofs (none found by grep); each must be green. Seal with `bin/cairn test --seal --timeout 900 cairn/machines/corrosion/proofs/test_corrosion_probes_report_to_the_watch.py <the probe-importing proofs>` (it runs each and writes its validation beside it). Commit with message '6c75219037b5: corrosion probes report to the watch' (the commit runs the reseal ladder, so allow an hour); commit the commons.

A ticket is standing when parse_workflow(doc["workflow_and_state"]).here (cairn.tools.base.transitions) is "PROVED" or "WATCHME"; a ticket whose workflow_and_state does not parse is skipped (except Exception: continue), exactly as the template does.

API, read 2026-10-03: PROBE.payload({}) (cairn/tools/base/probe.py, Probe.payload) runs the probe's carry over that context and returns the dict watch_carry builds — keys "ticket" (the 12-hex id), "holds" (bool) and "finding". watchme_spec_error(doc) (cairn/tools/base/watchme_spec.py) returns None when the ticket's watchme satisfies the rule and a refusal string otherwise; the receiver tooth asserts it returns None after the receiver is added.
